It attributed minor revenue timing shifts to temporary supply-chain congestion and multi-phased project execution, ended the quarter with USD 5.6 billion liquidity and net cash, and raised full-year guidance to USD 13.8-14.2 billion sales, USD 6.65-6.75 adjusted EPS, and USD 2.4-2.6 billion adjusted free cash flow.

Vertiv's Q2 Form 10-Q confirms the VRT Class A common-stock identity on NYSE and reports USD 2.811 billion cash, USD 300 million short-term investments, USD 2.940 billion long-term debt, USD 2.484 billion unused revolver capacity, and covenant compliance. Inventory rose to USD 2.523 billion and receivables to USD 3.750 billion, while deferred revenue reached USD 3.634 billion; disclosed risks include backlog conversion, large-customer terms, fixed-price execution, supply chain, tariffs, capacity expansion, competition, and geopolitical disruption.
